reading.body:
Sam Liccardo's AI record mixes legislative action with money from the largest AI companies, and the two run on the same calendar. Across 19 dated events from March 2025 to July 2026, he cosponsored seven AI-related bills, voted yea on four, and received eight contributions from AI company and AI-focused political committees.

The contributions are small and consistent: $1,000 to $3,000 each, from Google, Microsoft, Meta, and Amazon PACs, spread across the period rather than clustered around any single vote or bill. The legislative activity is broader than the money. His cosponsorships include AI grid and energy measures, an AI education act, deepfake labeling, and financial services AI, which places him among members treating AI as a subject of governance rather than a single-issue concern.

The grid and energy bills are the most specific signal here. Two cosponsorships on the same day in February 2026 address AI cyber protection for grid infrastructure and international AI energy grid modernization. That connects AI policy to power and transmission, the constraint this site tracks, though the data records only that he signed on, not what the bills would do or whether they moved.

What the data does not show is causation or motive, and the page says so. Contributions and cosponsorships appear in date order, but nothing here establishes that money produced a position or that a vote followed a donation. It also does not cover committee assignments, floor statements, or any AI activity outside these 19 records, so it is a partial ledger, not a full picture of his record.

summary: Every dated AI event this site holds for Sam Liccardo: bills sponsored or cosponsored, recorded votes on AI bills, and money from AI company and AI-focused political committees, newest first. 19 events.
